papers.title: PERAN GURU DALAM MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI BELAJAR SISWA STUDI LITARATUR
papers.abstract: Declining mental engagement among students in the classroom often stems from how teachers design learning experiences, yet prior studies tend to examine instructional factors and environmental support in isolation. Addressing this conceptual gap, this article aims to re-examine the multidimensional role of educators in fostering student learning motivation through an in-depth literature review. Employing a qualitative approach with a narrative literature review design, literature searches were conducted across five academic databases for publications spanning 2022–2025. Staged screening following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol filtered 482 initial records down to 30 peer-reviewed journal articles as the final sample. Data were recorded via a data extraction sheet and processed using thematic-descriptive analysis. Thematic mapping yielded eight focus clusters integrated into five core dimensions of teacher roles: pedagogical and professional competence balancing classroom structure with autonomy, empathetic interpersonal communication, active learning strategies supported by digital media, effort-based positive reinforcement, and environmental management alongside family synergy. The systemic synergy of these five dimensions serves as a motivational ecosystem driver that fosters extrinsic drive while sustaining students’ intrinsic learning awareness. ABSTRAK Melemahnya keterlibatan mental peserta didik di ruang kelas sering kali berakar pada cara guru merancang pengalaman belajar, namun kajian terdahulu cenderung membedah faktor pengajaran dan dukungan lingkungan secara terpisah. Menjawab celah konseptual tersebut, artikel ini bertujuan menelaah kembali peran multidimensi pendidik dalam menumbuhkan semangat belajar siswa melalui penelusuran pustaka secara mendalam. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan rancangan narrative literature review, penelusuran literatur dilakukan pada lima pangkalan data akademik untuk publikasi periode 2022–2025. Seleksi bertahap berdasarkan protokol Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) menyaring 482 rekaman awal hingga menetapkan 30 artikel jurnal ilmiah sebagai sampel akhir. Data direkam melalui data extraction sheet dan diolah menggunakan analisis tematik-deskriptif. Pemetaan temuan menghasilkan delapan klaster fokus kajian yang terintegrasi ke dalam lima dimensi utama peran guru, meliputi kompetensi pedagogik dan profesional yang menyeimbangkan struktur kelas serta otonomi, komunikasi interpersonal empatik, strategi belajar aktif berbantuan media digital, penguatan berbasis proses usaha, serta pengelolaan lingkungan dan sinergi keluarga. Sinergi sistemik kelima dimensi tersebut terbukti menjadi penggerak ekosistem motivasi yang menumbuhkan dorongan ekstrinsik sekaligus merawat kesadaran belajar intrinsik siswa secara berkelanjutan.

papers.title: Preoperative optimisation before revision total hip arthroplasty: a systematic review of modifiable risk factors and optimisation strategies
papers.abstract: Introduction Revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) is associated with perioperative morbidity and healthcare utilisation. Preoperative optimisation may improve outcomes, but revision-specific evidence remains poorly defined. Objective To evaluate preoperative factors and optimisation strategies associated with rTHA outcomes and identify areas where evidence for active intervention remains lacking. Methods PubMed, MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to September 2026 for primary studies evaluating preoperative optimisation, modifiable risk factors or related interventions in adults undergoing rTHA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and PROBAST principles. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. Results The search identified 226 records; 103 remained after 123 duplicates were removed, and 15 studies were included. No randomised controlled trials were identified. Anaemia was the most consistently investigated potentially modifiable factor and was associated with transfusion, complications, prolonged length of stay and readmission. Hypoalbuminaemia, chronic opioid exposure, depression, obesity, impaired functional status, renal dysfunction, liver disease and cardiopulmonary comorbidity also identified higher-risk patients. An opioid-free interval was associated with attenuation of excess risk in one observational study. Fast-track pathways reduced length of stay, although readmission remained high. No eligible study directly investigated structured preoperative physiotherapy or exercise-based prehabilitation specifically before rTHA. Conclusion Multiple potentially modifiable preoperative factors are associated with adverse outcomes following rTHA, with anaemia demonstrating the most consistent revision-specific evidence. However, current literature is predominantly retrospective and prognostic, and evidence that active correction of identified risks improves outcomes remains limited. Prospective interventional studies, particularly of multimodal optimisation and exercise-based prehabilitation, are required.

papers.title: Cemented Versus Uncemented Bipolar Hemiarthroplasty for Displaced Femoral Neck Fractures in Older Adults: A Prospective Observational Study from a Tertiary Care Center in India
papers.abstract: Open Access Original Research Paper Cemented Versus Uncemented Bipolar Hemiarthroplasty for Displaced Femoral Neck Fractures in Older Adults: A Prospective Observational Study from a Tertiary Care Center in India Authors: Dr. Karan Keshav Malave¹, Dr. Piyush Jagannath Sawale², Dr. Abhijit Dagduba Sapkal³* ¹Senior Resident, Lokmanya Tilak Municipal Medical College and General Hospital, Sion, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. ²Senior Resident, HBT Medical College and Dr. R. N. Cooper Municipal General Hospital, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. ³Senior Resident, Grant Government Medical College and Sir J. J. Group of Hospitals, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Corresponding Author: Dr. Karan Keshav Malave, Senior Resident, Lokmanya Tilak Municipal Medical College and General Hospital, Sion, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24387380 Received: 07 October 2026, Revised: 22 October 2026, Accepted: 07 November 2026, Online First: 22 November 2026 ABSTRACT Background: Displaced intracapsular fractures of the femoral neck in older adults represent a high-burden injury associated with significant mortality risk, prolonged disability, and loss of independent ambulation. Bipolar hemiarthroplasty remains widely adopted in many low- and middle-income settings because it offers predictable pain relief and functional restoration with lower cost and shorter operative time than total hip arthroplasty (THA). However, fixation choice for the femoral stem cemented versus uncemented remains controversial. Cemented stems may provide superior immediate stability in osteoporotic bone and potentially faster early recovery, but carry risk of peri‑cementation hemodynamic instability consistent with bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). Objectives: To compare perioperative safety and short-term clinical and functional outcomes of cemented versus uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty in adults older than 55 years with displaced femoral neck fractures, with emphasis on intraoperative blood pressure (BP) fall, early surgical site infection (SSI), pain, and functional recovery. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted over 18 months (January 2023 to June 2024). Forty‑one patients aged >55 years with displaced femoral neck fractures underwent bipolar hemiarthroplasty via a standardized posterior approach. Cemented fixation was performed in 23 patients and uncemented fixation in 18. Outcomes included intraoperative BP fall (none, 5–10 mmHg, >10 mmHg), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain at 6 weeks, SSI before suture removal, and Harris Hip Score (HHS) at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. Secondary functional indicators included limb length discrepancy (LLD), limp, ambulation status, walking distance, stair climbing, nail trimming ability, public transportation use, and sitting tolerance. Results: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Intraoperative BP fall differed significantly (p<0.001): “no fall” occurred in 1/23 cemented cases versus 15/18 uncemented cases; BP fall 5–10 mmHg occurred in 19/23 cemented versus 3/18 uncemented; BP fall >10 mmHg occurred in 3/23 cemented versus 0 uncemented. VAS pain at 6 weeks was similar (4.22±2.55 vs 5.06±2.15; p=0.272). SSI rates were comparable (2/23 vs 2/18; p=0.796). HHS did not differ significantly at 6 weeks (p=0.096), 3 months (p=0.356), or 6 months (p=0.169). LLD pattern differed (p=0.008), while most mobility indicators were broadly comparable. Conclusion: Cemented and uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty provided comparable short‑term functional outcomes up to 6 months. Cemented fixation was associated with markedly higher frequency of intraoperative BP fall, reinforcing the need for systematic BCIS‑aware anesthetic vigilance and cementation safety protocols. Keywords: femoral neck fracture; bipolar hemiarthroplasty; cemented; uncemented; Harris Hip Score; bone cement implantation syndrome; older adults; India INTRODUCTION Hip fracture is a sentinel injury in geriatric trauma and an increasingly important public health challenge. Beyond the immediate surgical episode, hip fractures often precipitate sustained declines in mobility and independence, increase caregiver dependence, and impose substantial costs on families and healthcare systems. Epidemiologic projections indicate that global hip fracture incidence will continue to rise sharply due to population aging and increased prevalence of osteoporosis and frailty, with a growing proportion occurring in Asia, including India (1,2). These trends have major implications for orthopaedic services, perioperative medicine, rehabilitation capacity, and long-term care infrastructure. Outcomes after hip fracture are shaped by both injury biology and the physiology of frailty. Older adults commonly present with multimorbidity, sarcopenia, cognitive vulnerability, and limited cardiopulmonary reserve. Consequently, immobility-related complications delirium, pneumonia, venous thromboembolism, pressure injuries, and functional deconditioning—represent major drivers of morbidity. Modern care models therefore emphasize timely surgery after optimization, coordinated multidisciplinary perioperative care, and early mobilization with a goal of immediate weight bearing where feasible. NICE guidance on hip fracture management highlights operating with the aim of allowing patients to fully weight bear without restriction immediately postoperatively and emphasizes consistent perioperative pathways and implant strategy (3). The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) similarly provides evidence-based recommendations for the management of hip fractures in older adults, with emphasis on coordinated care and appropriate procedure selection (4). Displaced intracapsular femoral neck fractures constitute a clinically distinct subset. Their intracapsular location disrupts femoral head blood supply and places union at risk, especially in osteoporotic bone. In older adults, internal fixation of displaced intracapsular fractures carries substantial risk of non‑union, avascular necrosis, and reoperation. As a result, replacement arthroplasty hemiarthroplasty or total hip arthroplasty (THA) is commonly recommended for many older patients with displaced intracapsular fractures. THA may offer superior functional outcomes in carefully selected, independently mobile patients; however, hemiarthroplasty remains widely used because it generally requires less operative time, is technically less demanding, and may have a lower dislocation risk in frail populations. In many tertiary care centers in India and other low- and middle-income settings, bipolar hemiarthroplasty remains a pragmatic and common option. Bipolar designs were developed to allow movement at an inner articulation, theoretically reducing acetabular wear and pain compared with unipolar constructs while remaining less resource‑intensive than THA. Even though acetabular erosion can still occur and some patients may later require conversion to THA, bipolar hemiarthroplasty provides reliable early pain relief and functional restoration for many older, low-demand patients. A central technical decision in hemiarthroplasty is the method of femoral stem fixation: cemented versus uncemented (cementless). Cemented fixation provides immediate mechanical stability, potentially improving early mobility and reducing postoperative thigh pain, particularly in osteoporotic bone. Multiple randomized trials and meta‑analyses report modest functional advantages and reduced mechanical complications such as periprosthetic fracture with cemented stems compared with uncemented stems (5–8). A major contemporary randomized trial found cemented hemiarthroplasty produced modestly better quality of life and lower periprosthetic fracture risk than uncemented fixation for intracapsular hip fracture (9). Conversely, uncemented fixation avoids cement-related physiological effects and may shorten operative time in some settings, but can be challenging in osteoporotic femora where press‑fit fixation is less reliable and may increase risk of mechanical complications (5–8). Cementation introduces unique physiological risk. Bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS) refers to a spectrum of peri‑cementation events including hypoxia, hypotension, arrhythmia, and in severe cases cardiovascular collapse. BCIS is particularly relevant to hip fracture surgery because patients are often elderly, frail, and comorbid (10). Professional safety guidance has therefore emphasized structured mitigation: preoperative risk stratification, enhanced monitoring, high inspired oxygen at cementation, adequate intravascular volume, clear team communication at cementation, and readiness for prompt vasopressor support (11). Within this context, prospective local data are valuable because outcomes depend not only on implant design but also on patient profile, anesthetic resources, rehabilitation intensity, and institutional protocols. The present prospective observational study therefore compared cemented versus uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty in adults older than 55 years with displaced femoral neck fractures at a tertiary care center in India, with emphasis on perioperative hemodynamics and short-term functional outcomes up to 6 months. Objectives 1. To compare functional outcomes after cemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty for displaced femoral neck fracture in older adults. 2. To compare functional outcomes after uncemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty for displaced femoral neck fracture in older adults. 3. To compare perioperative complications and early outcomes, with emphasis on intraoperative BP fall, SSI before suture removal, postoperative pain, and mobility-related functional indicators. papers.title: Parametric Non‐Intrusive Reduced Order Modelling via Taylor Series Neural Networks and Dynamic Identification
papers.abstract: Numerically solving parameterised partial differential equations (P‐PDEs) is both valuable and computationally intensive, driving the development of reduced‐order models (ROMs). Recently, methods that combine latent space identification techniques with deep learning algorithms (e.g., autoencoders) have shown great potential in describing the dynamical system in the lower‐dimensional latent space. In this paper, a new parametric latent identification of nonlinear dynamics neural networks, P‐TLDINets, is introduced, which relies on a novel neural network structure based on Taylor series expansion and ResNets to learn the parametric differential equations that govern the dynamics in the latent space. During the training process, Taylor series‐based Latent Dynamic Neural Network (TLDNet) and identified equations are trained simultaneously to generate a smoother latent space. In order to facilitate the parameterised study, a ‐nearest neighbours (KNN) method based on an inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation scheme is introduced to predict the identified ODE coefficients using local information. Compared to other latent dynamics identification methods based on autoencoders, P‐TLDINet eliminates the encoder‐decoder's dependence on spatial coordinates, enabling it to be a parameterised ROM. Additionally, its lightweight network structure allows high generalization capabilities with less training time. P‐TLDINet was tested on the 2D Burgers' equation and the lock‐exchange case, maintaining an error of less than 2% compared to high‐fidelity models.

papers.title: THE 2026 BRUCE SMITH SR. AWARD ADDRESS: Enhancing Our Mission to Deliver a Superior Educational Experience: Four Strategies
papers.abstract: The Academy of Criminal Justice Sciences is a professional organization whose mission is to promote education, research, and practice within the discipline of criminal justice. Its implicit purpose is to educate the next generation of practitioners, academics and policy analysts/decision-makers to advance the discipline and develop skill sets to promote democratic social control. This paper explores four strategies designed to do this in an educational environment. The four strategies discussed are: 1) Demonstrate relevance of criminal justice topics covered in a course that relate directly to the understanding of the justice system and its potential improvement; 2) Encourage classroom engagement through the use of active learning techniques; 3) Ensure involvement in the actual practices of the criminal justice system; and 4) Create a congenial learning environment. The paper concludes by discussing how the students’ educational experience can be evaluated and continually improved to generate the next generation of thoughtful and educated field professionals, academics/researchers and policy analysts/decision-makers.

papers.title: Enforcing continuous symmetry in physics-informed neural networks for solving the 1D wave equation
papers.abstract: As a typical application of deep learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) have gained significant attention in recent years as a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) under the paradigm of artificial intelligence for Science. However, improving their limited accuracy remains a major challenge for PINN. Symmetry-enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SPINN) embed the invariant surface conditions derived from the Lie symmetries of PDEs into the loss function of PINN, so as to improve the solution accuracy of PDEs. This paper is the first to extend SPINN to solve the 1D wave equation, and conducts a comparative analysis with PINN. Numerical experiments show that SPINN can effectively solve the 1D wave equation. Compared with the PINN method, SPINN demonstrates better performance and effectiveness, with its predictive accuracy improved by one to two orders of magnitude, exhibiting superior predictive precision and generalization capability.

summary_en.motivation: Improving the limited accuracy of physics-informed neural networks for PDE solving motivates the incorporation of physical symmetry constraints.
summary_en.method: The invariant surface conditions derived from Lie symmetries are embedded into the PINN loss to form SPINN, which is applied to the 1D wave equation and compared against standard PINN.
summary_en.result: SPINN solves the 1D wave equation effectively and improves predictive accuracy by one to two orders of magnitude over PINN with better generalization.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on the 1D wave equation benchmark the proposed method against standard PINN.

papers.title: Enhanced Finite Control Set‐Based Predictive Torque Control for Maximum Power Extraction in Wind Turbine System
papers.abstract: In large‐scale wind energy conversion systems (WECSs), three‐level neutral point clamped (3L‐NPC) converters, and finite control set model predictive control (FCS‐MPC) schemes are attractive for high‐power operation because of their direct switching control and fast dynamic response. However, the increased number of voltage vectors in the 3L‐NPC converter increases the computational burden of the conventional FCS‐MPC scheme. In addition, most current‐based predictive controllers mainly focus on ()‐axis current tracking, whereas maximum power extraction and stable generator operation are more directly associated with electromagnetic torque and stator flux behavior. To address these issues, this study proposes an enhanced model predictive torque control (EMPTC) strategy for improving the machine‐side converter performance of a 20 MW permanent magnet vernier generator (PMVG)‐based WECS. In the proposed method, a two‐stage prediction structure is used as a computationally efficient switching‐state selection framework. In the first stage, six virtual space vectors are evaluated using predicted machine current information to identify the suitable voltage‐vector region. Then, in the second stage, the final switching state is selected from the corresponding real voltage‐vector candidates using a multi‐objective cost function based on predicted electromagnetic torque, stator flux, and switching frequency. Moreover, capacitor voltage information is used for the conditional selection of small voltage vectors in Stage II, thereby supporting neutral point voltage balancing without its influence in the cost function. The proposed controller is validated in MATLAB/Simulink under step and randomly varying wind speed conditions and compared with existing FCS‐MPC schemes. The comparison results show that the proposed EMPTC improves torque generation, power extraction performance, and steady‐state behavior while reducing the switching‐state evaluation burden for PMVG‐based large‐scale WECS operation.

llm.why_not_core: This paper applies model predictive control to wind turbine power electronics and contains no surrogate modeling, no FEA/FEM data, no design optimization, and no biomechanical or implant context.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低三电平变流器有限集模型预测控制的电压矢量计算负担并提升风电最大功率提取。
summary_zh.method: 提出两阶段预测转矩控制，先筛选虚拟矢量区域再用多目标代价函数选定开关状态。
summary_zh.result: 在阶跃与随机风速下改善了转矩、功率提取与稳态性能并减少开关状态评估量。

summary_en.motivation: Conventional finite control set model predictive control for three-level converters suffers from high computational load and neglects torque and flux behavior relevant to maximum power extraction.
summary_en.method: A two-stage predictive torque control scheme first narrows the voltage-vector region using predicted currents and then selects the switching state via a multi-objective cost function on torque, flux, and switching frequency.
summary_en.result: The proposed controller improves torque generation, power extraction, and steady-state behavior while reducing switching-state evaluation burden compared with existing FCS-MPC schemes.
summary_en.validation: The strategy is validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations under step and randomly varying wind speed conditions against baseline FCS-MPC controllers.

papers.title: Fixed-Wing versus Multirotor UAV Recognition from Radar Track Kinematics Using a Jump-Markov Multiple-Model Estimator
papers.abstract: Recognising whether a small unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is of fixed-wing or multirotor type is a prerequisite for threat assessment and countermeasure selection in counter-UAS surveillance, yet many deployed surveillance radars provide only plot-level kinematics without micro-Doppler signatures. Falileev and Shatovkin (2020) proposed recognising the UAV type from track kinematics alone, exploiting the fact that only rotary-wing platforms can hover for a sustained period: a three-mode jump-Markov system (manoeuvre, non-manoeuvre, hover) is estimated with a second-order generalised pseudo-Bayesian (GPB2) filter, and a rotary-wing declaration is issued when the hover mode is estimated on n consecutive scans within the same azimuth sector. This paper restates that algorithm in a reproducible form, analyses its transition probability matrices (TPMs), and evaluates it by Monte Carlo simulation over 1,300 synthetic radar tracks at a 3 s update period. We show that the published TPMs are not row-stochastic and, once normalised, have identical rows, i.e. they describe a memoryless mode process that cannot accumulate evidence over scans. In our simulations the published parameterisation never declared a multirotor (0/600 tracks, measurement noise 1–25 m). Replacing the TPM with a diagonally dominant, persistence-aware matrix yields 100% recognition of multirotors at every noise level with a median latency of 9–12 s after hover onset and at most 1% false declarations on nominal fixed-wing tracks, against a median latency of 6–63 s for a filtered speed-threshold baseline. For low-airspeed fixed-wing aircraft flying into strong headwinds, a horizontal-velocity gate on the mode-conditioned estimate reduces false declarations from 38% to 8% (3-of-3 rule) at a cost of 3 s median latency. We discuss the latency–false-alarm trade-off governed by n and the fundamental limits of kinematics-only recognition.
papers.venue: International Journal of Science Architecture Technology and Environment

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究雷达航迹运动学对无人机类型的识别，与增材制造生物医学材料、多孔结构、LPBF 或骨整合完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper contains no additive manufacturing, no porous lattice design, no mechanical testing, no fatigue analysis, and no biomedical or implant context whatsoever.

summary_zh.motivation: 在仅有航迹运动学、缺乏微多普勒特征的监视雷达下识别无人机类型。
summary_zh.method: 复现三模态跳变马尔可夫模型与GPB2滤波，并分析转移概率矩阵。
summary_zh.result: 原参数化无法识别多旋翼，改用持续性矩阵后识别率达100%且误报率低。
summary_zh.validation: 基于1300条合成雷达航迹的蒙特卡洛仿真。

summary_en.motivation: UAV type discrimination is needed for counter-UAS threat assessment when radars supply only plot-level kinematics without micro-Doppler cues.
summary_en.method: The authors restate a three-mode jump-Markov estimator with a GPB2 filter, analyze its transition probability matrices, and propose a persistence-aware replacement matrix.
summary_en.result: The published parameterization never declared a multirotor, whereas the revised matrix achieved full multirotor recognition with low false-alarm rates and short latency.
summary_en.validation: Evaluation relied on Monte Carlo simulation over 1,300 synthetic radar tracks at a 3 s update period.
